bullets.text: The Tamil Nadu government set an October 15 deadline for Chennai flood mitigation and monsoon-preparedness works after finding several incomplete projects.
Citizens in Velachery, Porur and Ponneri faced power outages on September 30 due to major shutdowns announced by TNPDCL.
Residents in Vadaperumbakkam staged a midnight road roko protesting a power outage, arguing with police and electricity board officials.
News channels discussed potential risks associated with artificial intelligence alongside political updates concerning Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam.
Passengers expressed disappointment as trains continue to skip the Adambakkam railway station along the Velachery-St Thomas Mount MRTS extension.
Drinking water supply was restored in Adyar and Perungudi zones following the completion of major pipeline relocation work.
Chennai recorded 62 dengue cases in a single day, prompting the GCC to intensify mosquito control measures in Anna Nagar and Adyar.
Two people drowned in separate incidents along the Thiruvallur and Chennai coasts, involving a mason in Pulicat and a college student.
A sudden fire broke out at the Tiruttani Murugan temple during the lighting of ghee lamps, causing concern among devotees.
Heavy rain and lightning in Tiruttani caused a transformer to tilt and low-lying areas to flood, disrupting normal life.
TIDCO invited tenders to set up a Rs 400 crore digital financial hub in Coimbatore to promote the fintech sector.
An IIT Madras study revealed that even educated professionals fall victim to digital financial scams due to various vulnerabilities.
CtrlS Datacenters partnered with Ciena to build five high-capacity metro networks connecting nine data centres across several Indian cities including Chennai.
The Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam administration faced scrutiny after rolling back several controversial announcements made since taking office.
TVK flags suddenly appeared on encroachment shops along the GNT Road in Gummidipoondi ahead of an eviction drive.
Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay will share the stage with Prime Minister Narendra Modi in Chennai on October 11.
Commuters received a shock as announcements detailed specific stations where metro trains will not stop along the Vadapalani-Poonamallee line.
